newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Rato says Spain met 1996 deficit target.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Rato says Spain met 1996 deficit target.

text.p: Spanish Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said on Wednesday that Spain had met its 1996 target for the public deficit.
The government had forecast it would bring the public deficit down to 4.4 percent of gross domestic product in 1996 and to three percent this year.

"The government has for the first time reached the public deficit target and has, in addition, shifted the direction of public spending considerably and therefore after three years of public deficits of above six percent, in 1996 it was at 4.4 percent (of GDP)," Rato told an economic conference.
Rato said deficit reduction and the decline in inflation were the two most important successes of the conservative Popular Party government, which assumed control of government last year.
